bugs.text: `pressed` is declared const (167) and reassigned (`pressed={}`) at 302 and 315 under 'use strict'. The first update() step throws TypeError 'Assignment to constant variable'; frame() (765-771) never reaches draw() or the next requestAnimationFrame, so the game freezes on the title screen. Enter, movement, sound: nothing works. Confirmed by result.json (pageerror at t=0, starts=false) and five identical screenshots.

killEnemy sets e.state='dead' (563) before every check of e.state==='dive'/'beam' (568, 570, 571, 581). Consequences if the game ran: diving enemies always score formation points (50/80/150; 100/160/400/800/1600 never awarded) and a captured fighter is always destroyed, never freed, so rescue, docking and the dual fighter (541-552, 583-584) are dead code.

Goei escorts are set to state 'escort' and positioned only while their boss is in 'dive' (513-514). When the boss finishes its dive (t>=1 at 504) and enters 'return' or 'beam', the escorts stay frozen in 'escort' state, usually below the screen (y=H+34/H+46), where upward shots cannot reach them. They are released only if that boss is later killed (577), and a second dive of the same boss overwrites e.escorts (470), orphaning them for good: the stage can then never clear (433). Latent, since the game never runs.
Beam end condition `!beamNodes&&G.muted&&e.beamT<3.4`: when muted, beamStart (146) creates no nodes, so the tractor beam would end after 0.1 s instead of 3.5 s.
captiveShoot computes an aimed vx, but the enemy-bullet update only applies vy, so captive shots would fall straight down instead of toward the player.
While being pulled up by the beam the ship is drawn with the normal white/blue palette (sprPlayer); it only turns red once held (sprCaptured at 696). Spec says it turns red when caught.
The shot cap checks `G.shots.length<2` before a dual fighter fires two shots, so three player shots could be on screen at once.
Wave bonus is added via addScore with a '1000' popup and announced with a second 'BONUS 1000' popup, so the two overlap.
In challenging stages no player-vs-enemy collision is checked, so the fly-through enemies cannot hit the player.
High score is updated live (324) but only written to localStorage after GAME OVER + 4 s (312); closing the tab mid-game loses it.

Leftover junk: an uncalled updateBullets with a 'placeholder removed below' comment and a broken integrator, a no-op `G.hits===G.hits`, `G.ftime+=0`, and a setInterval hack that advances G.ftime only on the title to blink the prompt.

summary: As delivered the game is a frozen title screen: `pressed` is a const that update() reassigns every frame (167 vs 302/315), so the first fixed step throws, the rAF chain dies, and Enter, movement, sound and every state after 'title' are unreachable; the play-test confirms it (pageerror at t=0, starts=false, five identical screenshots). It is scored strictly by the rubric's rule that code which can never trigger earns nothing, which is why nearly every gameplay item is 0 although the code for it is present. Read as a design, the file is a compact (777 lines), reasonably organised Galaga with most of the spec sketched in: Catmull-Rom entry paths in five groups, sway and breathing, boss dives with escorts, a widening animated tractor beam with capture and a captive held above the boss, challenging stages with waves and the hit-count screen, badges in arcade denominations, synthesized sounds and a proper accumulator loop; on that reading it would score in the mid-60s. But even with the const bug fixed it carries two serious logic faults: killEnemy marks the enemy dead before reading its state, so diving points and the rescue/dual-fighter mechanic never happen, and escorts get stranded off-screen so a stage can fail to clear. Sprites are small but recognisable and the title screen looks the part; code quality is middling, with several no-op lines and an uncalled leftover function suggesting the file was never run before being handed in.
